instruction: Move the dir4 directory from ~/Desktop/dir3/ into ~/Desktop/dir1/.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);
import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click(960, 540); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent was given an infeasible task to copy directory hierarchy using undefined variables $sourceDir and $targetDir. Spent 31 turns systematically checking environment variables, config files (.bashrc, .profile), searching with grep/find across home directory and system files. Correctly determined the task was infeasible and reported [INFEASIBLE].
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate terminal, run bash commands (grep, find, ls, cat), check environment variables, search config files systematically, use shell pipes and redirection
metadata.task_rationale: Tests directory move operation using the same dir1/dir3 structure from setup. Model demonstrated strong terminal skills, so moving directories is within capability. Partial credit rewards knowing the target even if source cleanup is missed.
metadata.explanation: Task requires moving dir4 from ~/Desktop/dir3/ into ~/Desktop/dir1/. Custom getter checks both locations: dir4 should exist in dir1 (moved to) and not exist in dir3 (moved from). Partial credit: 0.5 for dir4 in dir1, 0.5 for dir4 removed from dir3.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly checks both source and destination paths for the move operation: /home/user/Desktop/dir1/dir4 (destination) and /home/user/Desktop/dir3/dir4 (source)
Metric correctly implements partial credit: 0.5 for dir4 present at destination, 0.5 for dir4 absent from source, fully covering move semantics
Complete coverage: both aspects of a move operation (existence at target, removal from source) are verified
No postconfig needed since filesystem state persists after the operation
Minor issue: metric function ignores the 'expected' parameter and hardcodes comparison values ('YES'/'NO'), which works correctly but couples the metric to this specific task
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using the 'expected' parameter in the metric function instead of hardcoding 'YES'/'NO' comparisons, e.g.: if result.get('dir4_in_dir1', '').strip() == expected.get('dir4_in_dir1', 'YES')
